title: Explosion damages the Crimean Bridge across the Kerch Strait
body:
On 8 October 2022, at about 6:07 a.m. Moscow time, a bomb on a truck exploded on the westbound road lanes of the Crimean Bridge, which links Russia to the Crimean peninsula across the Kerch Strait. Spans of the road bridge fell into the water. A train carrying fuel tankers on the adjacent rail bridge caught fire and seven tankers burned. Five people died, including the truck driver and four people in a nearby car.

Russian officials and a senior Ukrainian official described the cause as a truck bomb, although the BBC suggested a maritime drone was more likely. Ukraine did not immediately claim the attack, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said his government had not ordered it. In July 2023, Deputy Defense Minister Hanna Maliar acknowledged that Ukraine had carried it out to disrupt Russian logistics, and the Security Service of Ukraine confirmed this.

On 9 October Vladimir Putin called the event an act of terrorism devised and ordered by Ukrainian special services. On 11 October the FSB said it had detained eight people. Rail traffic on the undamaged track resumed almost immediately, and the road bridge reopened to a single lane of light traffic later on 8 October. It was fully reopened on 23 February 2023, and the rail bridge on 5 May 2023.
